summary: The cited flag-halfspace theorem and its recursive identity apply to each finite Borel restriction after affine identification. The support-affine reduction and flag lifting are valid; a query outside the support affine space has a zero-mass flag. A nonzero continuous normal makes every charged fiber boundary H_d-null. For a pure-base normal, the lattice kernel is saturated even for irrational alpha, so it is primitive in Z^n, its real span has exactly the claimed lattice points, and passing to the affine hull of the positive boundary fibers strictly lowers lattice rank. The recursion terminates with at most q_0 pure-base layers after the explicitly stated suppression of support-null padding, including the possible terminal pure-base zero-mass layer. Iteration gives the claimed disjoint layer-mass decomposition, the singleton is null because d is positive, and no slice-heaviness estimate is asserted or used.
